caption: A glass of water sits on top of a large subwoofer, and when the music starts the water's surface breaks into fine ripples.

sa.check: A glass of water is present.
It sits on top of a large speaker or subwoofer.
The surface is flat first and breaks into ripples at a moment, when the music starts.
The ripples are fine and small, not a big slosh.

pc.expect: The rippling is driven by the speaker: the surface goes from flat to rippled when the music starts, and stays rippled while it plays.
pc.fail: The speaker's cone plainly pumps and the water stays mirror-flat; or the surface is rippled from the start and goes flat while the cone is pumping; or the ripples appear and vanish at random with the cone unchanged.

pc.expect: The glass itself stays put or creeps only slightly; the water's ripples are fine and stay within the glass; nothing else moves without cause.
pc.fail: The glass slides off or jumps; or the water sloshes in one big wave with the glass still; or ripples appear on other surfaces in the room.

pc.expect: The ripples are a pattern on the water's surface: fine concentric or crossing waves, droplets at most; the water stays in the glass.
pc.fail: The water jumps out in large spouts; or stays as a rigid textured surface that does not move; or the glass ripples along with the water.

pc.expect: Any droplets thrown up fall back and the water surface stays level overall.
pc.fail: Droplets hover above the surface; or the water surface tilts and holds; or water climbs the glass walls.

pc.expect: One glass and one speaker; the glass keeps its shape and the water its amount.
pc.fail: A second glass appears; or the water level jumps; or the glass sinks into the speaker; or the glass vanishes.

pc.expect: Everything in view, named in the caption or not, keeps its number, identity and shape unless something visible acts on it, and nothing passes through anything else.
pc.fail: An object that nothing visible acts on appears from nothing; or vanishes while still in frame and not occluded; or duplicates or merges with another; or turns into a different object or a different shape between frames; or any object passes through another. Changes brought about by the caption's event or by a visible interaction, objects leaving the frame, and occlusion are not failures.

pc.expect: The speaker's grille, the glass and the background stay the same.
pc.fail: The speaker changes design; or the glass changes shape; or the background shifts.

note: Sound is inaudible in the frames. The timing anchor for P1 is a visible cone, indicator light or the caption's implied start; ripples with no visible driver are not a violation on their own.
